purpose: Reconstruct the registered and legally relevant property state at a specified historical date without projecting the current register backwards or treating a later entry as proof of an earlier state.
source_basis: Registration of Title Act 1964, including sections 31, 61, 85 and 90 as amended
Registration of Deeds and Title Act 2006
Land Registration Rules 2012 and applicable amendments
Tailte Éireann Land Registry records and copy/search services
reconstruction_rules: A target-date question must be answered from records and law applicable to that date.
A current folio is evidence of the current registered state and must not automatically be treated as a historical snapshot.
A later registration entry may provide evidence about a transaction but does not by itself prove every legal fact existing before the entry.
Where a historical state cannot be directly observed, the system must identify the inference and the evidence supporting it rather than silently presenting it as a recorded fact.
Historical registration dates, event dates and document dates must remain separate fields.
The law applicable on the target date must be distinguished from the law applicable when a later record was created.
If the relevant property was not registered at the target date, the system must route to the Registry of Deeds and other appropriate historical evidence rather than forcing a Land Registry answer.
Where an event crosses a statutory amendment or commencement date, the applicable transitional provisions must be checked.
Historical ownership, beneficial entitlement and registered ownership remain distinct questions.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: official folio/register entry dated or demonstrably effective at the relevant time
evidence_hierarchy.role: direct evidence of registered state within its scope

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: certified Land Registry instrument or official registration document
evidence_hierarchy.role: evidence of the dealing and documents underlying registration, subject to access rules

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: official historical search, map or registry record
evidence_hierarchy.role: supports property identity, registration status and historical reconstruction

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Registry of Deeds memorial/search where the property was dealt with in that system
evidence_hierarchy.role: evidence that a deed or transaction was registered; deed effect requires examination of the deed itself

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: private deeds, probate documents, correspondence or user-supplied documents
evidence_hierarchy.role: supporting evidence requiring identity, authenticity, relevance and property matching

conflict_handling: If two official records appear inconsistent, do not silently choose one.
Identify the dates, legal status and provenance of each record.
Determine whether the apparent conflict is temporal rather than substantive.
Route unresolved legal conflicts to the appropriate professional or court process.
A later corrected or rectified register must not erase the fact that an earlier state existed; preserve the historical audit trail.
guardrails: Never use the current folio as a substitute for a historical register state without explaining the limitation.
Never infer that the person currently registered was necessarily the person registered on an earlier date.
Never infer a registration date from the date of a deed alone.
Never infer the legal effect of a Registry of Deeds memorial without examining the underlying deed where required.
Never treat a title plan as conclusive of boundaries; section 85 expressly limits the conclusiveness of the register/map description as to boundaries or extent.
Never collapse event date, document date and registration date.
Never publish a historical property conclusion without a property match and evidence chain.
official_routes: Tailte Éireann Land Registry copy/search services
Tailte Éireann Registry of Deeds search services
Court records where a court order is part of the title history
